text: A fictional portfolio case · Learning design
PRINT STUDIO
Designing a first visit
Prototype only · No measured participation outcome
The brief
Help a newcomer start making.
Cedar Print Studio wanted a first session that felt approachable without turning creative…
THE CONSTRAINT
One facilitator. Shared equipment. A 50-minute introduction. No requirement to speak in front…
My contribution
I designed
The arrival instructions, the first-task card and the sequence for trying the tools.
We decided
A facilitator reviewed the sequence. A studio technician checked the proposed equipment setup.
I did not own the venue, equipment approval or later programme delivery.
The turning point
Give the first task a clear boundary.
The initial concept offered every tool at once. In the fictional review, the facilitator…
I proposed one two-colour print before opening the rest of the studio.
This is a design rationale, not evidence of improved learning.
The first-task card
MAKE A PRINT
One shape. Two colours.
1 Choose a paper shape
2 Try a small ink test
3 Print, then change one thing
A concrete first action
The opening names something a newcomer can do immediately.
Permission to experiment
The last step frames a second attempt as part of making.
Editable prototype specimen · Wording and sequence have not been tested with learners
The tradeoff
Open choice
Guided start
More freedom at the start, with more tools and decisions to explain.
A common first task, with open exploration after the demonstration.
The proposed session uses a guided start. An experienced visitor can choose the open route.
A 50-minute session
ARRIVE + DEMONSTRATE
Show the tools and offer a written version of the task.
TRY ONE PRINT
Make a first attempt with optional facilitator support.
EXPLORE + REFLECT
Change one element; describe or write what happened.
